**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement sits at the **preferred** position for MINCOMMIT:

- **No take-or-pay.** Art. IX builds supply around Ono's *requirements*, not committed volumes. § 9.4(a) gives Ono the right "**but not the obligation**" to manufacture its own Materials, and § 9.4(b) gives Ono the "**right to obtain**" commercial requirements from Array. The binding obligation runs the other way — Array "shall supply Ono's reasonable requirements" (§ 9.4(b)(i)), which benefits us.
- **No minimum forecast or shortfall penalty.** Forecasting/ordering procedures are deferred to future clinical and commercial supply agreements (§§ 9.3(a), 9.4(b)(i)) with no minimum-volume or binding-order commitment reserved in this agreement.
- **Fees are usage-based.** Art. VI is an upfront licence fee, achievement-based milestones and royalties on actual Net Sales.
- **The one "shortfall" hit is benign.** p0430 is a year-end royalty reconciliation — precisely the true-up mechanic the playbook asks for, not a volume penalty.
- **Diligence ≠ volume commitment.** §§ 5.1(b)(iii) and 8.1(a) are Diligent Efforts commercialization standards, with an express carve-out that declining a study is not a diligence breach.

One item noted but deliberately not flagged here: the § 8.2 exclusivity-of-efforts covenant restricts Ono from commercializing Competing Products and has a post-termination tail. That is a competing-product restriction rather than a purchase minimum, it is drafted mutually, and it belongs under the exclusivity rule — flagging it here would double-count the same commercial term.

Watch-item for the supply agreement negotiation: because forecasting and ordering terms are pushed to the future Supply Agreement and must be "consistent with Array's contractual arrangements with its Subcontractors," a binding-forecast or minimum-order obligation could be introduced at that stage. Worth carrying MINCOMMIT forward as a checklist item when those agreements are drafted, but there is nothing to redline in this document.
